These findings indicate that N-Methylgitingensine may exert its biological effects through a series of interconnected pathways, where it acts as a modulator of the serine/threonine-protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit beta isoform, which in turn influences the activity of the target enzyme. The consistent scores across the three paths suggest a robust and reliable relationship, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence supports a plausible pathway where N-Methylgitingensine may regulate the activity of the enzyme through its interaction with the intermediate targets, though further experimental validation is required to confirm this hypothesis.
